ranking_reason: C first: every figure is arithmetic on one stated count (61), needing only one unnamed convention. A next: tiny surface but hangs on an unspecified canonicalisation. B last: three undefined conventions (obligation unit, coverage rule, percentage bases) make its headline numbers unreconstructable.
summary: Eight of the nine figures lack a stated recomputation convention; only 1830 (and 185 as its forced complement) follow from the text alone. The coverage rates admit exactly one consistent reading — 365 strict plus 205 permissive of 1259 gives 570 — yet no sentence states numerator, denominator or nesting.

findings.claim: "Across 60 constructions the corpus records 1259 functional obligations."
findings.problem: The counting unit is undefined: obligations per construction-row (shared obligation types counted once per construction) versus distinct types is never stated, nor is any dedup rule, nor what 'functional' excludes. Each choice moves 1259.
findings.falsifier: grep -n 'functional' bundle.md — the term occurs only in this sentence; neither the abstract nor any candidate defines it.
findings.fix: State the tally unit (row vs type), the dedup rule across constructions, and the exclusion defining 'functional'.

findings.problem: 'Covers' has no decision rule: exact element-name match, an alias/mapping table, or human adjudication are indistinguishable from the text. Whether approximate-fit rows count as covered determines 570 itself.
findings.falsifier: No passage in bundle.md defines 'cover'; the obligation-to-element mapping script or table would settle it and is not quoted.
findings.fix: Publish the match predicate and the mapping, and say explicitly whether approximate fits are inside the 570.

findings.claim: "The remaining 689 are residue: obligations for which the vocabulary has no name at all."
findings.problem: 689 equals 1259−570 only if coverage is binary. With a permissive/approximate category in play, the 205 approximate rows could sit inside either 570 or 689; the text asserts rather than defines the boundary.
findings.falsifier: Arithmetic 1259−570=689 holds, but no sentence classifies the 205 approximate rows relative to the covered/residue split.
findings.fix: One clause: approximate-fit rows belong to the covered count (or do not), making 689 mechanical.

findings.problem: Base and nesting unstated: percent of 1259? of rows? Does 'permissive' include strict or exclude it? The only arithmetically consistent reading is (365 strict + 205 permissive-only)/1259, which the reader must reverse-engineer; '205 rows' also switches unit from obligations to rows without remark.
findings.falsifier: 570/1259=45.27%, 365/1259=28.99%, 365+205=570 — consistent, but no sentence in bundle.md states any numerator or denominator.
findings.fix: Write the fractions out: '365/1259 strictly, a further 205/1259 permissively, totalling 570/1259'.

findings.problem: Beyond the shared base/naming gaps of F4, the strict/permissive distinction itself is never defined — what property makes a match 'strict' is nowhere said, so 29.0% cannot be recomputed even given the denominator.
findings.falsifier: Neither the abstract nor Candidate B defines 'strict'; the classification script would settle it.
findings.fix: Define the strict-match criterion in one sentence alongside the percentage.

findings.claim: "Sixty-one of the 72 protocols satisfy the requirements and warrants" (A: "61 satisfy the laws and warrants").
findings.problem: The satisfaction test is undefined — presumably self-admission of each protocol's own mechanism set into the agreement set, but the abstract never says how a concrete protocol is tested. A and C also name the predicate differently ('laws' vs 'requirements'), leaving identity of the conditions unconfirmed. 61 anchors 1830, 1645 and 185, so the ambiguity propagates through all of C.
findings.falsifier: The abstract defines the agreement set abstractly but states no test for a corpus protocol; the laws/requirements wording differs between Candidates A and C.
findings.fix: Define the satisfaction predicate once, fix one term, and note that the same 61 is used in A and C.

findings.claim: "Of the 1,830 unordered pairs among them, 1,645 compose to an admissible set and 185 do not."
findings.problem: Pair composition is underspecified: union of raw decompositions or of canonical forms, tested against which merged constraint set? Admissibility is defined for a set in the abstract, never for a pair operation, and the two input choices can move the count.
findings.falsifier: No sentence in bundle.md specifies the operands of pair composition; the composition script would settle it.
findings.fix: One sentence: pairs compose over canonical forms under the merged requirements, warrants and prohibitions of both partners.

findings.problem: As a number it is forced — 1830−1645=185, and the internal split 182+3=185 checks — so the arithmetic is unambiguous; flagged only to record that its meaning inherits F7's composition convention.

findings.claim: "Every failure arms a prohibition; requirements, warrants and grounding contribute none" and "attribution … resolves to 15 arcs and 10 elements with a strict below-set."
findings.problem: 'Grounding', 'arcs' and 'strict below-set' are used but never defined anywhere in the bundle; the attribution claim behind the 15/10 supporting figures is unrecomputable from the text.
findings.falsifier: grep -n 'grounding\|arc\|below-set' bundle.md — each occurs only in Candidate C with no definition.
findings.fix: Define grounding and the arc/below-set attribution machinery, or cite the script that computes them.

findings.claim: "29 have a canonical form strictly smaller than themselves"; the canonical form "omits exactly {Ct, Ex, Li}".
findings.problem: The canonicalisation operator is never specified — 'strictly smaller' presupposes a determinate closure procedure the bundle does not state, and the codes Ct/Ex/Li appear without a legend, so neither 29 nor the six-protocol signature can be independently reproduced.
findings.falsifier: Neither the abstract nor Candidate A states how canonical forms are computed or what the element codes denote.
findings.fix: Cite the closure rule (or committed script) producing canonical forms and include the element legend.

findings.claim: B reports "15 constructions are inadmissible" (of 60) while A and C report 61 of 72 satisfy the laws/warrants.
findings.problem: The relation between these partitions is never stated: since admissibility adds the prohibition class, the 15 could lie inside the 61, but with different scopes (60 vs 72) and counts (15 vs 72−61=11) a reproducer cannot reconcile the bundles' figures without one connecting sentence — it reads as drift even if benign.
findings.falsifier: Abstract: admissibility = agreement set ∩ prohibition class; no passage links B's 15 to A/C's 61.
findings.fix: State whether the 15 inadmissible constructions satisfy the laws and warrants, and on which population (60 or 72) each count is taken.

strongest_candidate_argument: Every C figure is one arithmetic step from the stated 61 — C(61,2)=1830, 1830−1645=185, 182+3=185 — so a single stated composition convention would make the entire result independently reproducible.
dissent_note: Quality lenses may rank B first because the residue is the boldest claim; on reproducibility it is the least checkable. Others may treat 45.3%/29.0% as rescued by their internal consistency, but a recovered convention is still a guessed one.
